triples.relationship: Narrative parallel: received strength followed by offense against God
triples.rationale: Hosea charges that those whose arms God strengthened devised evil against Him. Chronicles says Uzziah was wonderfully helped until he grew strong, then became proud and acted unjustly against the Lord; the earlier account names the Lord as the giver of his prosperity. Both contrast received strengthening with subsequent offense against its divine giver. Uzziah's specific sanctuary act is not assigned to Hosea's people, and Hosea's arms are not replaced by a particular military invention.
triples.source_text: and I strengthened their arms, but they devised evil against Me.

target_units.text: In Jerusalem he made machines devised by a designer to stand on the towers and corners for shooting missiles and large stones. Their construction was heard of far away, for he was wonderfully helped until he grew strong.
But when he grew strong, his heart was lifted up to destruction. He acted unjustly against the Lord his God and entered the Lord’s sanctuary to burn incense on the incense altar.

triples.relationship: Rhetorical parallel: challenging alternative helpers in destruction
triples.rationale: Hosea asks who will help Israel in destruction, between declaring that no one saves apart from God and challenging the king to save them. Deuteronomy similarly challenges trusted gods to arise and help, then declares that no god is beside the Lord and no one can deliver from His hands. Both questions expose the insufficiency of rival sources of rescue when God judges. Hosea's immediately challenged king is not equated with Deuteronomy's foreign gods.
triples.source_text: In your destruction, Israel, who will help?

target_units.text: And the Lord said, Where are their gods, in whom they trusted,
whose sacrifices’ fat you ate, and whose drink offerings’ wine you drank? Let them arise and help you, and become your protectors.
See, see that I am, and there is no god beside Me. I will put to death, and make alive; I will smite, and I will heal; and there is none that shall deliver out of My hands.
